title: bee herding run --continue: follow-up rounds through the same mailbox
action: Per D3 (round-numbered results): add --continue <job-id> to bee herding run — reuses the EXISTING job mailbox: reads the highest result-N.json, renders the round N+1 brief via the mailbox module (round number explicit), sends it with herdr agent prompt to the job's recorded pane/agent (persist pane+agent identity into job.json at spawn so --continue can address it), then runs the same poll loop waiting for result-(N+1).json with the same idle-timeout/ceiling/pane-lifecycle flags. Refuses typed when the job dir is missing, has no prior result, or the pane is gone. --continue with --dry-run renders the round N+1 brief and sends nothing. Update the registry entry only if its flags block executes examples (keep examples[0] unchanged and green). Seam tests with FakeHerdr: continue sends prompt (never agent start), waits on the incremented round, refuses on missing job/result/pane.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml herding && PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test registry_dispatch

truths: --continue sends herdr agent prompt with the round N+1 brief and never calls agent start
--continue waits on result-(N+1).json, not the already-present round N
Missing job dir, missing prior result, or dead pane each refuse with a typed error
